outcome.answer: Yes — [1] directly matches this idea by reducing communication in split learning through local error signals instead of propagated gradients. [1] says the client uses an auxiliary classifier at the split point, the server trains on transmitted activations, and backward gradients are no longer sent, cutting communication roughly in half. [7] is a partial match: it routes global error signals in a dual-stream architecture without transporting transposed forward weights, but it is about biologically plausible learning rather than shared neural architectures in general.
